evidence:
# Dense radial prefixes can still have an explicit strongly convex interpolant

Status: complete candidate argument, unverified; no new verifier allocation.
This is a diagnostic counterexample to treating radial crowding as a genuine
legality obstruction, and a new explicit interpolation tool. It does not
solve the unrestricted exact-profile comparison. Accepted1252b8823bb5a290
is used only for maximal completion and its anchor representation.

## 1. Direct interpolation on a Lipschitz graph

Let finitely many planar points (s_i,t_i), including (0,0), lie on the graph
t=phi(s) of a globally piecewise-linear continuous function phi with
phi(0)=0 and Lipschitz constant ell>=0. Let z=alpha+i beta, with beta real,
and suppose

    mu=alpha-|beta|(2ell+1)>0,
    L_g=alpha+|beta|(2ell+1)<=1.                               (1)

Define on the entire real plane

    f(s,t)=alpha(s^2+t^2)/2 + beta s t
                 -2beta integral_0^s phi(v) dv.                (2)

Then f is mu-strongly convex, has L_g-Lipschitz gradient, is minimized at
zero with value zero, and has

    grad f(s_i,t_i)
       =(alpha s_i-beta t_i, beta s_i+alpha t_i)
       =z(s_i+i t_i).                                         (3)

Indeed the gradient everywhere is

    (alpha s+beta t-2beta phi(s), alpha t+beta s),

which is continuous. On every linear piece of phi its Hessian is

    [[alpha-2beta phi'(s), beta], [beta,alpha]].

For an arbitrary vector (a,b), the discrepancy of this quadratic form from
alpha(a^2+b^2) has absolute value at most

    2|beta|ell a^2 +2|beta||ab|
       <=|beta|(2ell+1)(a^2+b^2).

Thus each Hessian lies between mu times the identity and L_g times the
identity. Integrating along any line segment, divided at the finitely many
vertical break lines of phi, gives global strong convexity and the gradient
Lipschitz bound. A segment lying in a break line has constant s and the same
bound directly from the gradient formula. Its gradient at zero is zero,
so strong convexity makes zero the global minimizer. Substitution of
t_i=phi(s_i) proves (3). In particular ALL ordered interpolation conditions
hold for the actual values f(s_i,t_i); no value is assigned independently.

If these points are x_i=P_i(z), P_i the ordered schedule-prefix polynomial,
then (3) gives the actual GD recursion. Their Gram matrix is the ordinary
real Gram matrix in the plane. Rotating all points first is also allowed,
since scalar complex multiplication commutes with a planar rotation.

## 2. Independent every-cycle estimate for the same graph geometry

For any simple directed cycle through these points, put Area_C and Energy_C
as the signed area sum and squared-edge sum. Then

    |Area_C| <= (ell/2) Energy_C.                              (4)

To prove this, write consecutive vertices as (a,phi(a)) and (b,phi(b)).
The area sum equals

    sum_(a->b) (a-b)(phi(a)+phi(b)),

since its additional diagonal terms telescope. Also the oriented integrals
sum_(a->b) integral_a^b phi(v)dv vanish. Piecewise integration by parts gives

    (b-a)(phi(a)+phi(b))-2integral_a^b phi(v)dv
        =integral_a^b (2v-a-b)phi'(v)dv.

Its absolute value is at most ell(b-a)^2/2, in either orientation. Summing
over the cycle and using (b-a)^2<=the squared Euclidean edge length proves
(4). It has no dependence on the number of points in a radial annulus.

## 3. An explicit family with every prefix point in one annulus

For every integer n>=1, take the n unit steps h_i=1 and define

    z_n=1/(2n)+i/(10n),
    c_n=1-z_n,
    x_i=c_n^i=s_i+i t_i,      i=0,...,n,
    g_i=z_n x_i,
    x_star=g_star=0.

All these n+1 indexed nonzero prefix points have radius in (1/2,1].
To see this, r=|c_n| satisfies

    r^2=1-1/n+13/(50n^2)<1,
    r^n>(1-1/(2n))^n>=1/2.

The last inequality is Bernoulli's inequality, or follows by induction
from (1-t)^n>=1-nt for0<=t<=1. Strictness follows from the nonzero imaginary
part of c_n. Thus their radial density count for this annulus is n+1.

Nonetheless these points and the origin lie on a graph of Lipschitz constant
ell=2/5, uniformly in n. Let theta=-arg(c_n)>0. Then

    n theta <= n/(10n-5)<=1/5.

Therefore s_i>0, t_i<=0, and

    rho_i=-t_i/s_i<=tan(1/5)<=2/5.

Here tan(t)<=2t on[0,pi/4], by the derivative bound sec^2(t)<=2. The real
parts strictly decrease because

    s_(i+1)-s_i=-s_i[1/(2n)+rho_i/(10n)]<0.

The slopes of successive prefix chords are

    (t_(i+1)-t_i)/(s_(i+1)-s_i)
       =[(1/10)-(1/2)rho_i]/[(1/2)+(1/10)rho_i],

whose absolute values are at most1/5 for0<=rho_i<=2/5. The segment from
the origin to x_n has slope -rho_n of absolute value at most2/5. Define phi_n
by piecewise-linear interpolation through the points in increasing real
coordinate order

    (0,0), x_n,x_(n-1),...,x_0=(1,0),

and extend it by zero outside[0,1]. This is one explicit globally continuous
piecewise-linear function with Lipschitz constant at most2/5 and phi_n(0)=0.

Use (2) with alpha=1/(2n), beta=1/(10n), and phi=phi_n. Formula(1) yields

    mu=8/(25n),  L_g=17/(25n)<=1.                             (5)

We therefore have an explicit fixed convex1-smooth strongly convex function
f_n, on the real plane, with exactly the displayed unit-step orbit and with
all the stated real data simultaneously legal. This is not a formal moment
matrix or pairwise-only interpolation argument.

## 4. One orthogonal terminal vector and a free-terminal lower value

Let F_n be the maximal interpolant of these actual prefix jets, as provided
by accepted1252b8823bb5a290. For j in I={star,0,...,n}, set

    v_j=f_n(x_j), y_j=x_j-g_j, delta_j=v_j-|g_j|^2/2,
    H(v)=|v|^2/2+max_(j in I)(<y_j,v>-delta_j), F_n=H^*.

Pointwise maximality and (5) give

    H(v)<=f_n^*(v)<=|v|^2/(2mu).

Define D=x_n-(<x_n,g_n>/|g_n|^2)g_n and w=mu D. This same vector satisfies
<w,g_n>=0 and |D|^2=|x_n|^2/26. EVERY anchor obeys

    2delta_j+2<x_n-y_j,w>-|w|^2
         >=2<x_n,w>-|w|^2/mu=mu|D|^2.

Consequently, for every real b,

    2F_n(x_n-bg_n)>=mu|D|^2
           = [8/(25n)] |c_n|^(2n)/26
           >1/(325n).                                       (6)

We used |c_n|^(2n)>1/4. The same bound follows for f_n itself directly from
strong convexity and the minimum distance from the origin to the line
x_n-b g_n. Thus one fixed function handles every b; the endpoint gradient
is unconstrained.

## 5. Precise diagnostic consequence

For this legal spectral point, the sufficient radial-density test

    (alpha-mu_0)(1-alpha)-beta^2
        >=6M|beta|(1-mu_0),                                  (7)

with M=n+1, fails for EVERY proposed0<mu_0<1. If mu_0>=alpha its left side
is negative. If mu_0<alpha, the left side is at most alpha=1/(2n)<=1/2,
while the right side is greater than or equal to

    (3/5)((n+1)/n)(1-1/(2n))>=3/5.

Thus radial crowding cannot be used to infer illegality or weakness of the
full complex-prefix ansatz. The complete graph interpolant above remains
legal and has an order1/n free-terminal payoff despite density n+1.

Unit-step schedules already have stronger standard scalar lower witnesses;
(6) is a diagnostic calibration, not a claimed improvement for them. The
new structural input is the graph geometry and its explicit nonseparable
interpolant, which avoids a point-count loss. Extending it to recurrent
prefixes with multiple overlapping graph branches, while preserving all
old gradients and values, remains open.

# Exact joint repair of an individually illegal complex mode

Status: complete candidate calibration, unverified; no new fact_submit.
Accepted inputs are1252b8823bb5a290 for interpolation/maximal completion
and dfde2fa326c908bf for the complex cycle calculation. This is a concrete
three-dimensional object opening the remaining mixed-mode branch; it is
not a quantitative arbitrary-horizon profile theorem.

## 1. A specified normal operator and the complete real prefix

On R^3 define the fixed real normal operator

    A=[[1/2,-2/5,0], [2/5,1/2,0], [0,0,1/2]].

Thus its first plane is complex multiplication by z=1/2+(2/5)i and its last
coordinate is multiplication by lambda=1/2. Use the single prefix step
h_0=1 and the exact real vectors

    x_0=(1,0,1)/sqrt(2),
    g_0=(1/2,2/5,1/2)/sqrt(2)=A x_0,
    x_1=(1/2,-2/5,1/2)/sqrt(2)=x_0-g_0,
    g_1=(41/100,0,1/4)/sqrt(2)=A x_1.

The squared spectral weights are1/2 and1/2, |x_0|^2=1, and all inner
products come from this one real Euclidean Gram matrix. Include the optimum
jet x_star=g_star=0, f_star=0. Prescribe

    f_0=5/16,  f_1=3/40.

Here are the complete quantities needed to check legality:

    |g_0|^2=33/100,
    |g_1|^2=|g_0-g_1|^2=1153/10000,
    <x_0,g_0>=1/2,
    <x_1,g_1>=<g_0,g_1>=33/200.

For the signed interpolation residual
Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+|g_i-g_j|^2/2, all SIX ordered inequalities are

    Q_(0,star)=-9/400,      Q_(star,0)=-59/400,
    Q_(1,star)=-647/20000,  Q_(star,1)=-347/20000,
    Q_(0,1)=-697/20000,     Q_(1,0)=-297/20000.                (1)

Each is strictly negative. These numbers follow by substituting the
displayed inner products, x_1-x_0=-g_0, and f_0-f_1=19/80. Thus every
ordered smooth-convex interpolation condition holds on the SAME data.

## 2. One spectral component is nevertheless illegal

The unweighted complex component has points

    X_0=1, X_1=1-z=1/2-(2/5)i, X_star=0,
    G_j=z X_j.

Here alpha=1/2, beta=2/5, sigma=|z|^2=41/100, and
kappa=alpha-sigma=9/100>0. Consider the cycle X_0->0->X_1->X_0. Its
signed area sum and edge energy are

    Area=2/5,  Energy=1+41/100+41/100=91/50.

The exact interpolation cycle weight from accepteddfde2fa326c908bf is

    beta Area-kappa Energy/2
      =4/25-(9/100)(91/50)/2
      =781/10000>0.                                         (2)

Therefore NO function values can make this individual complex prefix
legal. Its pairwise cocoercivity coefficient kappa is positive, so the
failure is a genuine multi-point cycle, not merely a negative real part or
a violation of the two-point optimum condition.

The scalar component lambda=1/2 is individually legal, but the actual joint
values in(1) are not obtained by a separable interpolation of the two
components: the first such component does not exist. Joint legality in(1)
is therefore strictly more permissive than legality of every mode.

## 3. Fixed maximal interpolant and a uniform free-terminal witness

For j in I={star,0,1}, put y_j=x_j-g_j and delta_j=f_j-|g_j|^2/2. Then

    y_0=x_1, y_1=x_1-g_1, y_star=0,
    delta_0=59/400, delta_1=347/20000, delta_star=0.

Define, explicitly,

    H(v)=|v|^2/2+max_(j in I)(<y_j,v>-delta_j),
    F(x)=sup_v(<x,v>-H(v)).

By(1) and accepted1252b8823bb5a290, F is globally convex differentiable
1-smooth, interpolates every listed jet, has minimum zero at zero, and is
the pointwise maximal interpolant of this fixed prefix.

Choose the one fixed real terminal vector

    w=(0,-1/(16sqrt(2)),0).

It satisfies

    <w,g_1>=0,
    |w|^2=1/512,
    <x_1,w>=<y_0,w>=<y_1,w>=1/80.

For EVERY prefix anchor the affine lower score is therefore

    star:  2delta_star+2<x_1-y_star,w>-|w|^2
              =1/40-1/512=59/2560;
    j=0:   2delta_0+2<x_1-y_0,w>-|w|^2
              =59/200-1/512;
    j=1:   2delta_1+2<x_1-y_1,w>-|w|^2
              =347/10000-1/512.

The first is the minimum, since1/40<347/10000<59/200. Evaluating the
conjugate at this same w, for any real b, gives

    2F(x_1-b g_1)
      >=2<x_1-b g_1,w>-2H(w)
      =min_(j in I)[2delta_j+2<x_1-y_j,w>-|w|^2]
      =59/2560.                                             (3)

The function, weights, prefix values and w are fixed before b is selected.
No final gradient has been forced to equal A(x_1-b g_1).

## 4. The exact joint-cycle interface for further work

For any finite list of complex modes z_l=alpha_l+i beta_l and fixed weights
w_l>=0 summing to one, define real direct-sum points and gradients by

    x_i=(sqrt(w_l)P_i(z_l))_l,
    g_i=(sqrt(w_l)z_l P_i(z_l))_l,
    x_star=g_star=0,
    kappa_l=alpha_l-|z_l|^2.

The complete interpolation edge weight is the sum of the individual edge
weights. Consequently its cycle weight is exactly

    sum_l w_l[beta_l Area_C(z_l)-kappa_l Energy_C(z_l)/2].       (4)

The joint data admit values if and only if(4)<=0 for EVERY directed cycle.
Necessity follows by summing interpolation inequalities. For sufficiency,
remove nonpositive cycles from paths to the optimum, let ell_i be the
maximum such path weight, set f_i=-ell_i, and apply the finite interpolation
construction of accepted1252b8823bb5a290. This argument checks the joint
values; it does not posit independent functions for each mode.

Equation(4) is recorded as an interface, not as the missing quantitative
answer. The concrete data in Sections1--3 demonstrate that its additional
freedom is real. To repair the recursive-family obstruction, a chosen
finite family of modes and weights must control all cycles over the whole
horizon and retain a benchmark-scale free-terminal payoff. No such
arbitrary-horizon quantitative construction is established here.

while the reverse adjacent inequality requires

    v0-v1>=5781/20000.

But the first two permit at most4219/20000. The difference is
1562/20000=781/10000>0. This is a positive triangle cycle, so no values
can realize the circular prefix. The elliptic repair uses no added mode or
dimension; a different common real metric alone changes legality.

## 2. All cycles for one fixed metric

For any nonnegative schedule h and complex z=alpha+i beta with beta!=0,
define real coordinate vectors

    r_i=(Re P_i(z),Im P_i(z)),
    v_i=B r_i,         B=[[alpha,-beta],[beta,alpha]],
    P_i(z)=product_(t<i)(1-h_t z),
    r_star=v_star=0.

Choose one real symmetric positive definite matrix M with M_11=1. A real
invertible T with T^T T=M exists by diagonalizing M and taking square roots
of its positive eigenvalues. Set x_i=T r_i and g_i=T v_i. These are actual
real vectors, ||x0||=1, and the GD recursion holds for the supplied schedule.

For an ordered edge j->i define

    q_ij=v_j^T M(r_i-r_j)+(v_i-v_j)^T M(v_i-v_j)/2.

Let sym(X)=(X+X^T)/2. Then q_ij=tr(M C_ij), where

    C_ij=sym((r_i-r_j)v_j^T)+(v_i-v_j)(v_i-v_j)^T/2.       (2)

Thus existence of legal values is equivalent to the simultaneous conditions

    tr(M sum_(j->i in C) C_ij)<=0                         (3)

for EVERY directed simple cycle C on {star,0,...,n}. The same M is used
throughout; its three entries cannot vary with the cycle or the time index.

Here is the complete sufficiency argument. If(3) holds, every closed walk
has nonpositive total edge weight by deleting successive simple cycles.
For each i let ell_i be the maximum q-weight of a directed path i->star.
The maximum exists among simple paths, because removing a nonpositive cycle
does not lower a path weight. In particular ell_star=0. Put f_i=-ell_i.
Appending an edge j->i to a maximizing path from i to star gives
ell_j>=q_ij+ell_i, hence f_i>=f_j+q_ij. These are exactly all the required
ordered smooth-convex interpolation inequalities. The accepted maximal
construction produces a real fixed legal F. Conversely summing such value
inequalities around any cycle proves(3).

## 3. A geometric form that exposes the anisotropy

Define the real symmetric matrices

    S_M=(B^T M+M B)/2,
    K_M=S_M-B^T M B.

For a cycle C let Area_C=sum_(j->i in C) det(r_j,r_i). Expanding the edge
and telescoping its symmetric potential gives the exact identity

    sum_C q_ij
       =[beta tr(M)/2] Area_C
          -(1/2)sum_C(r_i-r_j)^T K_M(r_i-r_j).             (4)

To check the skew term, put J=[[0,-1],[1,0]]. Then
B=alpha I+beta J, JM+MJ=tr(M)J, and
(B^T M-MB)/2=-beta tr(M)J/2. Since r_j^T J r_i=-det(r_j,r_i), its
contribution is exactly the first term of(4). The symmetric part of each
edge is half the difference of r_i^T S_M r_i and r_j^T S_M r_j, minus
half the quadratic increment; the potential differences cancel on a cycle.

The reversed cycle has the same quadratic increments and the opposite
area. Thus the full condition is equivalently

    sum_C(r_i-r_j)^T K_M(r_i-r_j)
                  >= |beta| tr(M) |Area_C|               (5)

for every unoriented simple cycle. In particular every two-point cycle
requires (r_i-r_j)^T K_M(r_i-r_j)>=0. This is only positivity on actual
chord directions; it does not imply K_M is positive semidefinite.

For explicit parameter calculations,

    K_M=(alpha-alpha^2)M
        +beta(1/2-alpha)(M J-J M)-beta^2 adj(M),
    tr(K_M)=(alpha-|z|^2)tr(M),                           (6)

where adj(M) is the2x2 adjugate. The identity J M J=-adj(M) verifies(6).
When M=I, (5) reduces exactly to the circular area/energy condition in
accepteddfde2fa326c908bf.

For the explicit repair in Section1, M=diag(1,1/4), alpha=1/2, beta=2/5,
and

    K_M=diag(21/100,-39/400).

It has a strictly negative eigenvalue, but its quadratic form is positive
on every actual nonzero chord: the horizontal chord gives21/100 and the
two remaining chord directions(+/-1/2,2/5) give369/10000. The all-cycle
test is satisfied as certified by the six explicit value inequalities.
Replacing actual chord positivity by global positive semidefiniteness of
K_M would incorrectly discard this legal example.

## 4. Recursive copies preserve one common metric

For H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,b_j,H_j), let p_j be its full polynomial and
R_j=p_j(z)(1-b_j z). Induction on the actual ordered queries shows that
the multiset of positions of H_m is

    { product_(j=0)^(m-1) R_j^(epsilon_j) : epsilon_j in{0,1} }.

The left copy has the old positions, while the right copy multiplies them
all by R_(m-1). This identity retains multiplicities and query chronology
when the binary choice is read from the recursive tree.

Fix a cycle inside H_r. Every copy of H_r in H_m is obtained by multiplying
its coordinates by a product of R_j for j>=r. A nonreal z and real steps
make all these factors nonzero. If their product has argument theta and
modulus d, divide that copy's legal cycle inequality by d^2. It becomes
the SAME cycle inequality with metric R_theta^T M R_theta, where R_theta
is planar rotation. Averaging over all2^(m-r) copies is therefore legitimate
and retains a positive combination of actual full-prefix inequalities.

The isotropic part tr(M)I/2 is unchanged by this averaging. The two-dimensional
traceless part is rotated by twice each argument, and its norm is multiplied
by

    product_(j=r)^(m-1) |cos(arg R_j)|.                   (7)

This follows from averaging identity and rotation at each level: in a complex
coordinate for traceless symmetric matrices the multiplier is
(1+exp(2i arg R_j))/2, whose modulus is |cos(arg R_j)|. Formula(7) is an
exact possible bridge to a quantitative obstruction, not a claimed decay
bound. Resonant phase choices must be analyzed rather than silently excluded.

## 5. Retrieval and open quantitative step

Matlas returned unrelated statements in arXiv:1310.0717,1810.05847 and
1410.0486; none is used. No external theorem is imported. The fully legal
calibration is only one step; it does not establish a growing-horizon payoff.
The new task is to determine whether the metric repair persists quantitatively
on a specified recursive family. Formula(7) suggests testing phase averaging,
including exact resonances, while(5) keeps ALL cycles active on one metric.

# C91: a dense signed character law with a complete static realization

Status: **complete joint draft, UNVERIFIED**. This is the second newly
authorized analytical round, completed count23 after baseline21, reaching
ceiling23. The historical interruption is separate (attempted count24).
No computation, numerical evaluation, scan, replay, solver, installation,
subagent, or verifier call was used. The correctness predecessors are
accepted `1252b8823bb5a290` and `b98bb807d514e80d`. No assertion in the
unverified C90 manuscript is used as a proof premise.

This is a concrete new dense signed law/label geometry and a calibration
of its actual payoff. It does NOT improve the already accepted scalar
single-cut lower bound, prove an iterable improving child rule, or resolve
the original arbitrary-schedule exact-profile problem.

## 1. Original word and quantitative claim

Fix m>=4 and retain, throughout the whole construction,

    N=2^m, n=N-1, sigma=1+sqrt(2), delta=1-1/m,
    c_chr=sigma(1+1/m), a_chr=delta/c_chr,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a_chr*c_chr^j,H_j), 0<=j<m.

Use exactly h=H_m. Thus h_i=1+a_chr*c_chr^(nu_2(i+1)), 0<=i<n.
Every child has the same enclosing-m parameters. There is no reset,
padding, schedule permutation, or replaced bridge. For the proof write

    a=a_chr, ell=h_0=1+a, S=sum_(i<n)h_i,
    T=S-ell, q=a/(2T+1),
    mu=q/[64(1+S)^2].                                  (1)

Here a is a local abbreviation for a_chr, not the earlier single-cut
slope notation in the project glossary. The elementary bounds are

    6/25<a<1/2, ell<3/2, T>=1, 0<q<=a/3<1/6,
    0<mu<1/64, mu S<1.                                 (2)

All physical steps exceed one. The claim is an explicit convex
differentiable 1-smooth F_dense, with unique minimizer0, whose actual GD
on this word has true initial radius R_dense and satisfies

    V_dense=2F_dense(X_n)/R_dense^2
          >=(3/4) a^2/(2T+1),
    B_n V_dense>1/150.                                 (3)

The constant in (3) holds for EVERY m>=4 on the original words above.
It is a positive calibration, not the requested asymptotic factor one.

Its queried gradients have a strictly positive finite character law and
dense signed Gram matrix. In particular every later queried gradient has
negative correlation with g_0, and no two nonzero queried gradients are
orthogonal. This removes both premises behind the C89 selection mechanism.

## 2. Why simply adding independent coordinates fails

The scalar asymmetric Huber function

    phi_q(x)=x^2/2                     if x>=-q,
             -q x-q^2/2               if x<=-q          (4)

has continuous nondecreasing 1-Lipschitz derivative, unique minimizer0,
and is an instance of the accepted single-cut construction. From x_0=1,
the original first step ell sends it to -a. Its remaining gradients are
all -q and its final value has doubled gap a q=a^2/(2T+1).

On two different tail samples i<j, both ordered scalar interpolation
residuals are zero because that branch is affine. If one replaces a scalar
gradient z_i by (sqrt(1-epsilon)z_i,sqrt(epsilon)|z_i|e_i), uses the actual
same-step positions, and simply scales all values by 1-epsilon, the reverse
residual on such a pair becomes epsilon q^2>0. Thus the naive full-support
lift is NOT interpolable. This is an exact original-row obstruction to
that shortcut, for every epsilon>0.

The next sections supply and price the missing strict slack before adding
the independent coordinates.

## 3. A strict scalar function on the actual schedule

Define one scalar function, fixed before the run,

    f_mu(x)=(1-2mu)phi_q(x)+mu x^2/2.                  (5)

It is convex, differentiable, and has derivative Lipschitz constant
1-mu<1. Its curvature where defined is either mu or 1-mu. Its unique
minimizer is0. Write x_i for its actual GD trajectory from x_0=1 and
z_i=f_mu'(x_i). The first actual block is the physical leaf ell:

    z_0=1-mu,
    x_1=1-ell(1-mu)=-a+mu ell.                        (6)

For comparison define the unmodified Huber tail locations

    x_i^0=-a+q sum_(t=1)^(i-1)h_t, 1<=i<=n.

They lie in [-a,-(a+q)/2], so are at most -a/2. We now prove that all
actual x_i, i>=1, remain on the NEGATIVE FLAT branch of phi_q. Although
phi_q is flat in its derivative there, f_mu has the small positive
curvature mu, which is essential.

Put D_mu=2mu(1+S)=q/[32(1+S)]<q/32. As long as x_i<=-q, the true recursion is

    z_i=-(1-2mu)q+mu x_i,
    x_(i+1)=(1-mu h_i)x_i+(1-2mu)q h_i.              (7)

Writing d_i=x_i-x_i^0, it becomes

    d_1=mu ell,
    d_(i+1)=(1-mu h_i)d_i-mu h_i(2q+x_i^0).          (8)

All coefficients 1-mu h_i are nonnegative. Also
|2q+x_i^0|<=a+2q<1. Induction in (8) therefore gives
|d_i|<=mu(ell+sum_(1<=t<i)h_t)<=mu S<D_mu. Its own branch assumption is
preserved, since

    x_i<=-a/2+D_mu<-a/2+q/32
                       <=-47a/96<-q.                (9)

This proves (7)-(9) for every original sample, including n; it is not a
calculation on a reset or compressed tail. The closed formula, if desired,
is x_i=D+(x_1-D)product_(t=1)^(i-1)(1-mu h_t), where
D=(1-2mu)q/mu. Equations (6)-(7) specify all data without an optimization.

For i>=1 the gradients z_i are negative. Their magnitudes A_i=|z_i|
satisfy q/2<=A_i<=2q<1, using (2), (9), and mu<q. Also A_0=1-mu<=1.
Every tail step increases x_i by at least q/2 because h_i>1.
Consequently every pair of distinct sampled scalar positions, INCLUDING
the optimum0, is separated by at least q/2. For pairs involving the
optimum use |x_i|>=47a/96>q for i>=1 and x_0=1; for a pair involving
x_0 and a tail position use their opposite signs.

The actual doubled terminal value retains a quantitative fraction of the
known scalar payoff. Since both x_n and x_n^0 lie in the branch (4),

    2f_mu(x_n)>=(1-2mu)[a q-2q D_mu]
               >=(1-2mu)[a q-q^2/16]
               >=(31/32)(47/48)a q>(3/4)a q.         (10)

This explicitly prices the regularization and the change in trajectory.

## 4. Uniform strict slack for EVERY ordered scalar pair

For any scalar arguments x,y, put d=y-x and e=phi_q'(y)-phi_q'(x),
and set alpha=1-2mu. The necessary inequality in accepted
`1252b8823bb5a290` applied to phi_q says

    phi_q(y)-phi_q(x)-phi_q'(x)d>=e^2/2.

For f_mu, its gradient difference is alpha e+mu d. Expanding its signed
ordered residual gives

    Q_mu(x,y)
      =f_mu(x)-f_mu(y)+f_mu'(x)d
                            +[f_mu'(x)-f_mu'(y)]^2/2
      <=-alpha e^2/2-mu d^2/2+(alpha e+mu d)^2/2
       =-alpha mu(e-d/2)^2-mu d^2/4
      <=-mu d^2/4.                                    (11)

This holds in BOTH orientations, for every x,y, including zero.
Combining the actual sample separation with (11), define

    nu=mu q^2/16>0,
    epsilon=nu/[4(1+nu)] in (0,1/4).                  (12)

Every original scalar residual between distinct samples in
{star,0,...,n}, with star=(0,0,0), is at most -nu. Thus the smallest actual
nonempty block (6), its optimum incidences, both directions of every later
pair, and every terminal pair have a common explicit negative margin.

The displacement in (11) is the actual scalar displacement, equivalently
d=-sum h_t z_t between the corresponding chronological samples. The
signed contributions from the initial positive gradient and the later
negative gradients have not been changed or deleted.

## 5. Dense vector lift with all original pairs

Work initially in the Euclidean space R direct-sum R^N. Let e_i,
0<=i<=n, be its standard orthonormal vectors in the second summand.
Prescribe the full data by

    G_i=(sqrt(1-epsilon) z_i, sqrt(epsilon) A_i e_i),
    X_0=(sqrt(1-epsilon),0),
    X_i=X_0-sum_(t<i)h_t G_t,
    f_i=(1-epsilon)f_mu(x_i),                         (13)

and include the optimum jet (0,0,0). The first coordinate of X_i is
sqrt(1-epsilon)x_i. Its second coordinate is
sqrt(epsilon)Z_i, where Z_i=-sum_(t<i)h_t A_t e_t.

The original full residual splits EXACTLY, with the full signed scalar
displacement intact, as

    Q_ij=(1-epsilon)Q_mu(x_i,x_j)+epsilon R_ij.        (14)

For i<j finite, the added-coordinate residuals are

    R_ij=(1/2-h_i)A_i^2+A_j^2/2,
    R_ji=(A_i^2+A_j^2)/2.                            (15)

For an optimum pair, R_(i,star)=R_(star,i)=A_i^2/2,
since the i-th coordinate of Z_i is zero. As every A_i<=1 and h_i>=0,
ALL these residuals are at most one. Thus (11)-(12) prove the uniform
strict original-pair bound

    Q_ij<=-(1-epsilon)nu+epsilon=-3nu/4<0             (16)

on every distinct ordered pair of {star,0,...,n}. In particular (15) at
indices0,1 resolves the very first original physical block with its
genuinely negative correlation, before any appeal to a larger block.

This is a full pairwise calculation, not a covariance feasibility test.
The Gram and anchor products are

    <G_i,G_j>=(1-epsilon)z_i z_j+epsilon A_i^2 1_(i=j),
    <X_0,G_i>=(1-epsilon)z_i, ||X_0||^2=1-epsilon.    (17)

For all i>=1, <G_0,G_i><0. For every distinct pair, the product in (17)
is nonzero. Accordingly there is no orthogonal queried pair and no
nontrivial orthogonal component partition. The C89 history sign condition
fails, and its large orthogonal selection is absent. The negative skipped
terms are precisely (1-epsilon)h_t z_i z_t, which remain in (14).

## 6. An explicit positive finite character law and chronological labels

The same geometry is also a literal finite character construction.
Use d=m+1 bits and D_law=2^d=2N. Give physical sample i the label

    lambda_0=(0,binary(0)),
    lambda_i=(1,binary(i)), 1<=i<=n.                  (18)

The first bit records the sign, the other m bits record the original
physical index. The labels are distinct. They do not reorder or duplicate
any sample or insert any step.

Let s range over {0,1}^d, write e_sig for the vector with its first bit1
and all other bits0, and define

    chi_s(lambda)=(-1)^(s dot lambda),
    w_s=(1-epsilon)1_(s=e_sig)+epsilon/D_law.           (19)

Every weight is strictly positive and their sum is one. Define
u_i=(sqrt(w_s)chi_s(lambda_i))_s, and let eta_0=1, eta_i=-1 for i>=1.
Finite character orthogonality gives, with no positivity inference from
finite-field algebra,

    <u_i,u_j>=(1-epsilon)eta_i eta_j+epsilon 1_(i=j).   (20)

Therefore the actual gradients g_i=A_i u_i have exactly (17). This law
has dense correlation support: for every nonzero binary label difference
the kernel is (1-epsilon)(-1)^(its first bit), never zero.

For an entirely explicit anchor, including its true norm, put

    D_0=epsilon+(1-epsilon)N,
    lambda_extra=(0,binary(1)),
    v_s=chi_s(lambda_extra)/(D_law sqrt(w_s)),
    v_unit=v/||v||,
    Xhat_0=(1-epsilon)/D_0 sum_(i=0)^n eta_i u_i
                 +sqrt(epsilon(1-epsilon)/D_0) v_unit. (21)

The label lambda_extra is not one of (18). Pairing a differing bit proves
<v,u_i>=0 for every i. Also
sum_i eta_i<u_i,u_j>=D_0 eta_j. Equations (20)-(21) give

    <Xhat_0,g_i>=(1-epsilon)z_i,
    ||Xhat_0||^2=(1-epsilon)^2 N/D_0
                         +epsilon(1-epsilon)/D_0
                   =1-epsilon.                      (22)

Thus the anchor and gradients in (21) have the identical FULL Gram data
of (13), including the initial point. Set
Xhat_i=Xhat_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t and retain the values f_i in (13).
All original residuals (14)-(16) hold verbatim. The term involving v_unit
is an explicitly priced orthogonal component of the anchor, not an
unrecorded radius change. The dimension increase changes no time index.

## 7. ONE static function, exact values, unique minimizer, and true radius

Use either the direct-sum realization (13) or the character realization

    y_i=X_i-g_i, delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2,
    H_dense(v)=||v||^2/2
                    +max{0,max_(0<=i<=n)(<y_i,v>-delta_i)},
    F_dense(X)=sup_v(<X,v>-H_dense(v)).                (23)

The optimum row of (16) gives delta_i>=3nu/4>0. By accepted

an everywhere finite convex differentiable 1-smooth function satisfying
F_dense(X_i)=f_i and grad F_dense(X_i)=g_i at EVERY supplied sample.
Its actual GD is therefore exactly the original physical trajectory.
This uses one fixed function for the whole horizon, not changing
functions at a bridge.

Since every delta_i is strictly positive, H_dense(v)=||v||^2/2 in some
neighborhood of zero. It is everywhere at least ||v||^2/2, so
F_dense(0)=0. For any X!=0 choose a sufficiently small 0<t<1; then
H_dense(tX)=t^2||X||^2/2, implying
F_dense(X)>=(t-t^2/2)||X||^2>0. Hence

    argmin F_dense={0},
    R_dense^2=||X_0||^2=1-epsilon,
    V_dense=2(1-epsilon)f_mu(x_n)/(1-epsilon)
                =2f_mu(x_n).                         (24)

Thus the dense character lift preserves the strict scalar instance's
normalized payoff EXACTLY. The only loss from the known Huber calibration

inequality in (3), with actual values, minimizer and radius supplied.

For original smoothness L, replace F_dense by L F_dense and use physical

## 8. Comparison with the ORIGINAL exact benchmark

Here B_n is precisely the accepted Zhang--Jiang denominator
2S_bullet(n)+1, not 1+sum h or a newly defined profile. Recall from
accepted `b98bb807d514e80d` the original mass recurrences

    C_0=B_0=1,
    C_n=max_(0<=k<n)Omega(C_k,C_(n-k-1)),
    B_n=max_(0<=k<n)G(C_k,B_(n-k-1)),

The sum of the ACTUAL word has the exact closed form

    S=N-1+a_chr(c_chr^m-N)/(c_chr-2)

                  >9/1250>1/150.                    (29)

## 9. Explicit costs and the remaining mathematical gap

The new construction uses d=m+1 binary label bits, D_law=2N character

    nu=mu q^2/16=q^3/[1024(1+S)^2],

The smallest probability atom is epsilon/D_law. It may be very small;

## 10. Exact residual for xi=0; no unspecified optimization oracle

Set xi=0 for the explicit scalar interface below. Define

    h_c=e+2w, sigma=1-theta,
    R(sigma)=(K_c*sigma-h_c)/Lc,
    alpha_max=A/E_c,
    alpha_opt(sigma)=(u*v+2D*d)/(2D*Lc)
                              -d*h_c*sigma/(2w*Lc),
    Delta=u^2*v^2*w-d^2*e^2*D.                       (10.1)

These are closed formulas in the actual masses. R(sigma)>=0 is
sigma>=sigma0=h_c/K_c. The remaining sign conditions are EXACTLY

    R(sigma)<=alpha<=min(alpha_max,1-sigma),
    0<=sigma<=1,
    eta=[A-E_c*alpha]/Lc,
    beta=1-sigma-alpha, gamma=sigma, ell=alpha-R(sigma).

For a strict J22>0 certificate take sigma<sqrt(w/D). Its admissible
scalar interval is therefore

    sigma0<=sigma<sqrt(w/D),
    sigma<=1,
    sigma<=(h_c+Lc*alpha_max)/K_c,
    sigma<=(h_c+Lc)/(K_c+Lc).                         (10.2)

The latter two constraints ensure the alpha interval is nonempty.
At sigma0 it is nonempty and J22>0 by (5.6); this fact alone does
not guarantee PSD. Define alpha_clamp(sigma) to be alpha_opt if it
lies in that interval, and otherwise the nearer endpoint of the
interval (equivalently max(lower,min(upper,alpha_opt))).

Here is the exact determinant calculation. Set t_c=2Dalpha-A and
y_c=t_c-d*K_c/Lc. Equations (9.3)--(9.4) give

    J22=w-D*sigma^2,
    J11=[u^2*v^2+4d^2D(e+w)]/(4D*Lc^2)-y_c^2/(4D),
    J12=(sigma*y_c+d*h_c/Lc)/2.                      (10.3)

For the J11 constant, use

A*Lc*(u*v-d*U)+d^2*U^2=u^2*v^2.
Since K_c^2-U^2=4D(e+w), (10.3) follows by completing its square.
Expanding det J and completing the square in y_c gives the EXACT identity

    det J=(w-D*sigma^2)*Delta/(4D*w*Lc^2)
                         -D*w*(alpha-alpha_opt(sigma))^2.       (10.4)

Indeed the y_c-square coefficient is -w/(4D), its linear coefficient
is -sigma*d*h_c/(2Lc), and
4w(e+w)-h_c^2=-e^2; these yield precisely (10.4).

Consequently the following is the exact remaining inequality for

  Find sigma satisfying (10.2) such that

       <=(w-D*sigma^2)*Delta/(4D*w*Lc^2).              (10.5)
